status_definitions.documented: Explicit in the frozen source, not independently confirmed by organiser or official executable.
status_definitions.provisional: Selected development interpretation, with alternatives/questions retained.
status_definitions.deferred: No authoritative operational choice. Explicit policy returns UNVERIFIED and blocks a full-feasibility claim.

rules.title: Complete workload and yield
rules.decision: All activities must reach at least their required workload. Standard=1 and ECLO=1.5 units; surplus caused by the final indivisible access is permitted by >=. No dropping work.

rules.title: Earliest start week
rules.decision: Do not schedule before the planned-start week. Date-to-week conversion follows provisional R19; no intraweek start time is asserted.

rules.title: One access per activity per week

sources.anchor: Since an activity gets at most one access-night per week

rules.decision: Apply at most one activity access per week in all scenarios. The sentence appears in the C explanation but describes the activity granularity without a scenario qualifier.

rules.title: Working-span expansion

sources.anchor: A job that runs from one station to another must book every tunnel sector

rules.decision: For the supplied SEC endpoints, include every tunnel between them and all incident platforms on the same line/bound. Platform endpoints, reversed spans and disconnected/branching paths need explicit handling in Step 3; reject unsupported cases rather than invent a route.

rules.title: Legal sharing composition
rules.decision: Within one location/week/group: PM alone, one PC plus zero to three C, or one to four C. No PM+C, two PC, or fifth participant. Access type is independent of nature of works.

rules.title: Location capacity and excess accounting
rules.decision: Count distinct occupied groups per location/week, not activity rows. Excess is max(0, groups-supply), summed over location-weeks. A physical possession crossing three locations can therefore incur three excess units.

rules.title: Contract-local allocation indices
rules.decision: Use the supplied cap for (contract_number,activity_type,week). Indices are integers 1..cap. Equal indices in different contracts do not establish a common night.

rules.title: Local workfront limit
rules.decision: Count distinct activities per contract/type/week/access_night and enforce supplied workfronts. This check alone does not establish physical-night consistency (R10).

rules.title: Sharing-label scope
rules.decision: Labels are scoped to location and week. Never treat b1 as a globally named weekday or possession. Consistent renaming within each location/week leaves local accounting unchanged.

rules.title: Common physical night

sources.anchor: a works controller could dispatch against

rules.decision: Use local weekly accounting for the provisional benchmark model. Separately diagnose one-full-night-per-access consistency. Do not impose an unconfirmed global-night constraint on the benchmark or call local success dispatch-ready.
rules.enforcement_location: model adapter / future night diagnostic / UI

rules.title: Buffer class parameters
rules.decision: Read nature-of-works buffer counts from the supplied table: Live 2, Consist 1, Others 0; only Live requires opposite bound. These counts do not specify the whole expansion algorithm.

rules.title: Buffer geometry and terminal treatment
rules.decision: No authoritative selection between tunnel-hop/platform-edge interpretations. Request exact affected-location sets, including terminals. Until configured, protection coverage is unverified, not passed; do not run an all-rules-feasible claim.

rules.title: Live opposite-bound effect

sources.anchor: Live` mirrors closure to opposite bound

rules.decision: A Live closure affects the opposite bound. Whether and how the expanded buffer mirrors remains unconfigured with R12. Non-Live does not acquire this effect.

rules.title: Independent interchange capacity

sources.anchor: physically two adjacent tunnels, not one shared track

rules.decision: Prefer detailed section 2.2 and the supplied is_shared=0 rows over the opening shared-track narrative. ALP/BET tunnel and platform capacity remain separate; Live protection can couple them. Do not map fictional hubs to real stations.

rules.title: Live interchange trigger and footprint
rules.decision: Cross-line Live effects are required when applicable, but work-span versus buffer-contact triggering and exact propagation are unresolved. Require an explicit mapping before a complete protection check.

rules.title: Sharing exemption extent

sources.anchor: PC` and `C` are already buffer-free against each other

rules.decision: Provisionally recognise exemption only for the same group at the same location/week. Do not propagate A-B and B-C into A-C automatically or exempt every PC/C pair everywhere. Broader exemptions need confirmation; dependent protection checks remain unverified with R12/R17.

rules.title: Protection comparison time

sources.anchor: no external activity may enter it that night

rules.decision: Neither overlapping weekly footprints nor matching local labels alone proves simultaneity. Keep potential intersections as candidates. A definite temporal protection verdict requires a confirmed night relation or official weekly rule.

rules.title: Predecessor ordering
rules.decision: For a nonblank predecessor, provisionally require its entire workload to finish in an earlier week. Treat unknown IDs/cycles as input errors; do not silently drop dependency edges. Same-week sequencing is not representable yet.

rules.title: Calendar conversion and completion date
rules.decision: Use seven-day buckets anchored at horizon_start. Release week=floor((date-start)/7)+1. Completion=start+7*last_week-1 days; this matches all 14 sample results but does not prove hidden-date semantics. Out-of-horizon cases follow R21.

rules.title: Static supply repeats within horizon
rules.decision: Repeat each supplied location capacity in each in-horizon week. Zero is a real capacity; an absent location is an input error, not unlimited supply. Weekly overrides will be explicit future changes, not invented input columns.

rules.title: Horizon extension
rules.decision: Keep accesses in weeks 1..horizon_weeks until extension and its supply are authorised. Never invent extra weeks to hide infeasibility; report horizon-limited results as conditional.

rules.title: Scenario A policy
rules.decision: No supply excess and no ECLO. Delay may occur; objective interpretation is R28. Never relax workload or protection to produce a result.

rules.title: Scenario B policy
rules.decision: Planned completion is hard. Excess capacity is soft with no stated numeric ceiling. ECLO may occur in any week. Prose suggesting P3 slip in B conflicts with the explicit hard deadline; retain the hard deadline.

rules.title: Scenario C capacity policy

sources.anchor: up to 1 excess access-night per location-week

rules.decision: Allow at most one excess group per location/week above the supplied capacity, penalise every excess unit, permit delayed completion. Do not bake an additional supply increase into this allowance.

rules.title: Scenario C ECLO span and affected lines

sources.anchor: one continuous span of at most 2 calendar weeks

rules.decision: For each affected line, ECLO weeks must fit in at most two adjacent week buckets. Empty/single-week sets are allowed. Different lines choose independently; cross-line Live accesses must fit both. Determining affected lines depends on unresolved R15.

rules.title: ECLO penalty unit
rules.decision: Provisionally charge 5 per eclo=1 activity-access row. Also expose the count separately; do not deduplicate by local groups across locations and call that physical nights. The alternative physical-possession price remains open.

rules.title: Mixed ECLO flags within a shared group
rules.decision: Until clarified, require equal ECLO flags within a local sharing group. This is an explicitly stricter development choice, not a proven official constraint. Do not infer an extra ECLO award for a member flagged standard.

rules.title: Delay formula and metrics
rules.decision: Primary development score uses per-activity weighted planned-date lateness (100/10/1)*(1.3/1.2/1.0)*days. Separately report contract-day lateness and its contract-weighted total. A=delay, B=7*excess+5*ECLO, C=delay+7*excess+5*ECLO. Numeric scores remain provisional; unknown protection prevents a full-feasibility claim.

rules.title: Weighted priority versus strict precedence

sources.anchor: Contract tier decides which band you're in

rules.decision: Minimise the scalar penalty; do not silently impose lexicographic contract priorities or a fixed ECLO-before-capacity heuristic. Aggregate weighted trade-offs can contradict prose saying never delay higher tiers. Compare alternatives under the chosen formula, not the prose's incomparable batch-cost ratios.

rules.title: Occupancy export versus protection
rules.decision: Export work-span rows only as the sample does. Keep buffers/mirrors/cross-line effects in separate derived records; do not count them as extra submitted working rows without expander confirmation.

rules.title: Results aggregation and target date
rules.decision: One result per scenario/contract; complete at the maximum finishing week across its activities/types, using R19. Overrun=max(0, completion-planned_completion_date); keep contractual dates separate. Multiple project rows with conflicting planned dates require clarification rather than an arbitrary first match.

rules.title: Scenario input identity

sources.anchor: a Scenario C instance generated with amended, higher local supply

rules.decision: Develop A/B/C against the same frozen eight CSVs until another manifest is supplied. Label C input applicability provisional. Never edit the baseline or fabricate the amended C capacities.

rules.title: Output contract and unsupported instances

sources.anchor: hidden test instance (the 8 CSV instance files)

rules.decision: Three CSVs per scenario, exact documented columns. The eventual importer must accept supported unseen IDs/counts, not just the sample. Endpoint/category variations and solve-time limits still need organiser confirmation; reject unsupported structures clearly.

rules.title: No fabricated success under congestion
rules.decision: Persist in searching permitted alternatives, but distinguish timeout from proven infeasibility under selected assumptions. The brief's request not to declare impossibility cannot authorise dropping work, exceeding hard scenario limits or claiming an unchecked feasible result.

questions.question: Must every activity access use one common physical night over its full span, or does the judged model check local location/week packing only?
questions.requested_response: Return a physical-night assignment for Week 23 A001/A011, a corrected sample, or explicit confirmation of local-only validation. Equal at S16 and unequal at S15 cannot both hold under the full-night interpretation.

questions.question: Which field defines simultaneous work for a contract's workfront cap?
questions.requested_response: Explain Week 25 A040/A042 (C007 workfront=1, local nights 3/1, shared b4). State whether shared groups override local indices and supply expected pass/fail.

questions.question: Please specify the complete protection-expansion algorithm and export scope.
questions.requested_response: Return exact working/buffer/mirrored/cross-line location lists for E09-E11, including a terminal, a buffer touching an interchange, and direct hub work. Confirm platform inclusion, trigger, propagation limit, capacity treatment, and whether occupancy exports remain working-span-only as E24 shows. Confirm separate line capacities from section 2.2.

questions.question: Is the sharing exemption local to a group/location, pairwise across a possession, or transitive across linked groups?
questions.requested_response: Give a verdict for A-B at X and B-C at Y with an A-C protected intersection at Z. Clarify the scope of the PC/C buffer-free prose.

questions.question: How does the validator determine whether two protected footprints overlap in time?
questions.requested_response: Specify the comparison key or required night mapping. Give pass/fail for same night, different nights, and only weekly/group information. Do not rely on identical label strings across locations.

questions.question: Is predecessor_activity_id enforced, and may a successor start in the predecessor's finishing week?
questions.requested_response: Return E14 outcomes and treatment of cycles, unknown IDs, full-workload completion and same-week sequencing.

questions.question: What are the exact date-to-week and completion conventions?
questions.requested_response: Confirm partial-week planned starts, week-end completion, planned versus contractual overrun target, and contract aggregation across activity types. Supply a non-Monday start/non-Sunday deadline example.

questions.question: Does static supply repeat weekly, and may schedules extend beyond horizon_weeks?
questions.requested_response: Specify capacity/calendar beyond the horizon, missing-location handling and whether any actual weekday availability is supplied. Confirm extension policy separately for A/B/C.

questions.question: Which formula and priority policy are authoritative?
questions.requested_response: Return official sample metrics/objective and formula version: contract days 28 versus activity days 42 versus weighted activity 48.3. Resolve E21's 23.1 versus 14 delay score, E23's scalar versus lexicographic ranking, and the B hard deadline versus prose suggesting P3 slip. Confirm 7 per excess unit and 5 per ECLO unit; the heuristic table compares different batch quantities.

questions.question: How are ECLO yield, penalties and flags handled for co-sharing activities?
questions.requested_response: For two activities in one ECLO possession, state penalty 10 or 5 (or another documented rule), each activity's credited workload, and whether mixed 0/1 flags are legal. Define possession identity if used for deduplication.

questions.question: Which input files belong to A, B and C?
questions.requested_response: Provide authoritative scenario manifests/checksums or confirm all use the supplied eight files. If C has amended supply, provide that file; also provide B/C sample outputs if available.

questions.question: Please provide official tooling and the hidden-instance execution contract.
questions.requested_response: Provide validator/expander package or repository, version/commit, exact commands, sample validator JSON, limits on solve time/memory/file sizes and allowed schema/category/path variations. Confirm how an infeasible or timed-out instance should be reported without weakening hard constraints.
